title: Being the youngest in the band, and the union in the twenties
summary: He was usually the youngest man in older bands and got work by recommendation rather than through the union.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Was there -- did the young guys sort of hang together, and the older guys hang together, back in the twenties?

Well, it's hard to say, because as I remember back in the twenties, like I was -- in most bands I was in, I was the youngest man in the band. It's not like it is nowadays with these rock bands, where you all start out together.

See, when I -- all the bands I got in, they were men. And very few young musicians, you know. All of us were scattered in different bands and wasn't but, you know, just a few of us. So I would say we hung out with the
I see. Was the union strong then?
Did you get work through the union, or
No. Most of my contacts, I don't know, was through different people recommending me.
Well, you must have been a terror on tuba back then. You got an awful lot of work.
